summary: Nassau Valley Vineyards is described as the first winery in Delaware and currently the largest in the state. Its founder, jazz singer Peggy Raley, had to get the state legislature to pass a law allowing wineries before opening the vineyard in 1993. The winery was the only one in Delaware until Pizzadili Winery opened in October 2007, and it sits on eight acres catering to beach-bound tourists.
one_line: Nassau Valley Vineyards is Delaware's first and currently largest winery, founded in 1993 by jazz singer Peggy Raley.
key_facts: Nassau Valley Vineyards was the first winery in the state of Delaware in the United States.
Nassau Valley Vineyards is currently the largest winery in the state of Delaware.
Jazz singer Peggy Raley decided to open a winery in Delaware.
Peggy Raley first had to get the local state legislature to pass a law allowing wineries in the state.
By 1991, Peggy Raley had drafted the necessary legislation.
Peggy Raley obtained a license and opened Nassau Valley Vineyards in 1993.
Nassau Valley Vineyards was the first and only winery in Delaware until Pizzadili Winery opened in October 2007.
Nassau Valley Vineyards occupies eight acres of property at its site.
The winery caters to the beach-bound tourist traffic in the area.
